title: Genital Tuberculosis (GTB): Insights into Diagnosis, Treatment, Clinical Trials and Patents-A Comprehensive Review.
abstract: Genital Tuberculosis (GTB) represents a frequently unrecognized type of extrapulmonary Tuberculosis (TB) that affects the female reproductive system. The condition results in infertility, menstrual cycle disturbances, and pelvic pain. The condition is difficult to detect at an early stage because its mild symptoms can manifest in different body parts. Therefore, medical professionals require better methods for diagnosing and treating patients. This review aims to provide a comprehensive overview of the epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations, diagnostic approaches, therapeutic strategies, and current advancements in the management of GTB. The study presents information on New Drug Delivery systems (NDDs), current clinical trials, and new patents to guide future research. A literature-based narrative review was conducted, focusing on peer-reviewed articles, clinical studies, patents, and recent advances in diagnostics and therapeutics of GTB. The study focused on three main areas: anatomical site-specific manifestations; laboratory instruments and drug medications. The fallopian tubes are the most commonly affected site (90-100%), followed by the endometrium (50-60%), ovaries (20-30%), cervix (5-10%), while involvement of the vagina and vulva is rare (<1%). The diagnosis of GTB becomes problematic because both its visible and hidden symptoms start to appear. The development of effective detection methods depends on both traditional diagnostic methods and modern molecular methods, which include specialized laboratory equipment, imaging techniques, and histopathology. Current clinical trials and new patent approvals demonstrate the development of new methods for diagnosing and treating GTB, including improved therapeutic approaches and drug delivery systems. GTB presents both diagnostic and treatment difficulties because patients show different symptoms that can remain hidden. The combination of methods for diagnosing and treating GTB, through improved therapeutic approaches and drug-delivery systems, will enhance detection, treatment outcomes, and the ability to maintain fertility. The research should investigate personalized medicine approaches, molecular diagnostic technologies, and new therapeutic delivery systems to address the existing clinical needs in GTB treatment.

title: Hemorrhagic lumbar synovial cyst mimicking a neoplastic process: illustrative case.
abstract: Background Synovial cysts with extensive hemorrhage, marked mass effect, and tumor-like appearance are rare and may mimic neoplastic processes. Observations A 56-year-old man presented with progressive mechanical low back pain, neurogenic claudication, gait instability, and bilateral weakness. MRI revealed a 2.0-cm lesion arising from the right L3 facet joint, causing severe central canal and right foraminal stenosis with displacement of the cauda equina. Imaging features suggested pigmented villonodular synovitis. Intraoperatively, however, the lesion appeared fleshy, partially encapsulated, and dural adherent, resembling a nerve sheath tumor, with necrotic regions suggesting malignancy. Frozen-section analysis demonstrated benign fibroconnective tissue with marked reactive and degenerative changes, including necrosis and hemosiderin deposition, without evidence of neoplasia. Intraoperative confirmation of benign pathology shifted operative priorities toward anatomical preservation rather than extent of resection; gross-total removal was nevertheless achieved and the patient had complete neurological recovery. Permanent pathology was most consistent with a degenerative synovial cyst with hemorrhage. Lessons This case highlights the importance of integrating imaging findings, intraoperative appearance, and histopathological evaluation rather than relying on a single diagnostic modality. The combination of a focused differential and confirmation of benign pathology guided the extent of resection, balancing maximal lesion removal with preservation of adjacent structural elements. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26317.

title: Spindle cell oncocytoma: illustrative case.
abstract: Background Spindle cell oncocytoma (SCO) is a rare, nonadenomatous sellar tumor that often mimics pituitary adenomas both radiographically and clinically, making diagnosis and treatment difficult. Observations A 67-year-old male presented with fatigue and weakness, with MRI revealing an enhancing sellar mass with suprasellar extension and laboratory findings consistent with panhypopituitarism. He underwent endoscopic endonasal resection, which revealed a fibrous, highly vascular tumor adherent to surrounding tissue, consistent with SCO on final pathological analysis. Gross-total resection (GTR) was achieved, and the patient has been monitored regularly with no signs of recurrence at 9 months postoperatively. Lessons SCOs are an exceedingly rare entity often indistinguishable from pituitary adenomas preoperatively, yet their intraoperative hypervascularity and fibrous texture can complicate resection and predispose patients to recurrence. Accurate identification of these tumors and GTR when possible are essential to appropriate treatment. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26333.

title: Endoscopic transorbital approach for resection of Meckel's cave aspergillosis: illustrative case.
abstract: Background Aspergillosis involving Meckel's cave (MC) is rare. Only 5 previous case reports exist in the literature. The primary treatment for this disease is surgical debridement combined with antifungal therapy. The authors present a minimally invasive technique using an endoscopic transorbital approach (ETOA) to manage this condition. Observations A 26-year-old male corn farmer presented with progressive right-sided facial pain and numbness for 1 month. MRI demonstrated a markedly hypointense T2 signal lesion in the right MC with gadolinium enhancement. CT revealed sphenoid sinus opacification with bony erosion. Nasal endoscopy with sphenoidotomy and mucosal biopsy were noncontributory. He underwent an ETOA via lateral canthotomy. Irregular yellowish rubbery tissue adherent to all divisions of the trigeminal nerve was resected. Histopathological analysis confirmed septate fungal hyphae. The fungal culture identified Aspergillus flavus. After 6 months of voriconazole, the facial pain resolved despite persistent numbness, and MRI demonstrated radiological resolution of the lesion. The patient remained free of recurrence at 1 year. Lessons MC aspergillosis can present as trigeminal neuropathy in immunocompetent patients. The ETOA provides direct extradural access permitting tissue diagnosis and debridement without temporal lobe retraction. Combined with antifungal therapy, this approach may be a feasible strategy for this disease. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26736.

title: Postoperative epidural fluid collection mimicking epidural abscess: illustrative cases.
abstract: Background After craniotomy, fluid may accumulate in the surgical bed, raising suspicion for hemorrhage, abscess, or postoperative pseudomeningocele. Typically, peripheral contrast enhancement, internal restricted diffusion, and adjacent edema are consistent with infection. Observations The authors present 4 cases with postoperative epidural fluid collections mimicking epidural abscesses on MRI with restricted diffusion on diffusion-weighted imaging. Three of these cases were associated with adjacent brain edema. The fluid appeared 1-3 months after the surgery on routine follow-up MRI in the absence of clinical symptoms, and nearly resolved, either spontaneously without treatment or with conservative therapy alone. Given imaging findings concerning for infection in the absence of symptoms, diagnosis and management were challenging. Lessons When there is increased epidural fluid collection after craniotomy, radiographic findings may mimic abscess, but they are not always clinically significant. Clinical assessment is a crucial component of the diagnosis to avoid unnecessary intervention, and follow-up imaging is recommended. The pathogenesis of this restricting, enhancing fluid collection remains unclear. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26757.

The fluid appeared 1-3 months after the surgery on routine follow-up MRI in the absence of clinical symptoms, and nearly resolved, either spontaneously without treatment or with conservative therapy alone. Given imaging findings concerning for infection in the absence of symptoms, diagnosis and management were challenging.

Lessons

When there is increased epidural fluid collection after craniotomy, radiographic findings may mimic abscess, but they are not always clinically significant. Clinical assessment is a crucial component of the diagnosis to avoid unnecessary intervention, and follow-up imaging is recommended. The pathogenesis of this restricting, enhancing fluid collection remains unclear. https://thejns.org/doi/10.3171/CASE26757.

title: Proliferative Sarcoid Retinopathy With Bilateral Tractional Retinal Detachment.
abstract: A 28-year-old male patient without previously diagnosed systemic disease or any ocular history presented with 3 months of progressive blurred vision in both eyes. His ocular exam revealed bilateral vitreous hemorrhage, tractional retinal detachments (TRDs), and extensive retinal neovascularization (NV). His systemic workup revealed elevated angiotensin-converting enzyme, bilateral hilar, and mediastinal adenopathy on computed tomography (CT) chest scan, and extensive multifocal leptomeningeal-enhancing nodules within the posterior fossa on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) brain scan, confirming sarcoidosis with neurologic and ocular involvement. Ocular complications of sarcoidosis predominantly involve the anterior segment, with anterior uveitis as the most common presentation overall. While posterior findings of ocular sarcoidosis are less common, these include but are not limited to retinal periphlebitis with candlewax drippings, choroidal granulomas, and optic nerve involvement, with cystoid macular edema representing the leading cause of vision loss. This report presents a unique case of bilateral TRDs and retinal NV as the initial manifestation of sarcoidosis. Improved awareness of atypical ocular presentations of sarcoidosis is critical for facilitating earlier diagnosis and timely intervention.

title: Changes in Macular Area Following Epiretinal Membrane Removal and Its Correlation With Anatomical and Functional Parameters.
abstract: Background and objective This study aimed to evaluate changes in macular area after pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) with epiretinal membrane (ERM) peeling and determine correlations with visual acuity (VA) and optical coherence tomography (OCT)-based anatomical parameters. Patients and methods This retrospective study included 29 eyes with idiopathic ERM undergoing PPV and membrane peeling. Macular area was quantified using infrared images at baseline and 7 to 9 days, and 30 days and 3 months postoperatively. OCT parameters-including central macular thickness (CMT), inner retinal thickness (IRT), macular volume, disorganization of retinal inner layers (DRIL), and ellipsoid zone (EZ) status-were analyzed. Correlations between macular area change, VA (logMAR), and OCT parameters were assessed. Results Macular area significantly increased from 37.59 ± 11.67 mm 2 to 42.77 ± 10.92 mm 3 at 3 months ( P < .001). VA improved from 0.48 ± 0.19 to 0.20 ± 0.17 ( P < .001). CMT decreased from 508.68 ± 74.01 µm to 395.03 ± 63.62 µm ( P < .001). DRIL decreased from 82.8% to 31%. EZ disruption decreased from 37.9% to 17.2%; however, this change did not reach statistical significance (exact McNemar P = .070). Macular area change was not significantly correlated with visual acuity improvement at 3 months ( r = 0.081, P = .758), although macular area at 3 months was negatively correlated with CMT ( r = -0.560, P = .016). Conclusion Macular area expansion after ERM peeling appears to reflect structural recovery following release of retinal traction. Although some associations with visual outcomes were observed, independent prognostic value remains uncertain and requires confirmation in larger prospective studies.

title: Prediction of Acute Kidney Injury with Venous Excess Ultrasound (VExUS) Scoring Versus Renal Resistive Index (RRI) in Patients Undergoing On-Pump Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting: A Prospective Observational Study.
abstract: Background The diagnosis of acute kidney injury (AKI) using conventional markers such as serum creatinine and urine output is often delayed, prompting interest in bedside ultrasound-based predictors. This study compared renal resistive index (RRI) and venous excess ultrasound (VExUS) scoring for early prediction of AKI after on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Methods In this prospective observational study, 180 adult patients were enrolled. RRI and VExUS assessments were performed preoperatively and within 3 hours of cardiothoracic ICU admission. AKI was diagnosed within 48 hours postoperatively using kidney disease: improving global outcomes (KDIGO) criteria. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were constructed for RRI and VExUS parameters, and diagnostic accuracy was assessed using area under ROC curve (AUROC), sensitivity, and specificity. Results AKI occurred in 48 patients (26.7%). Postoperative RRI showed excellent discrimination for AKI (AUROC 0.854; cut-off ≥0.68: sensitivity 75%, specificity 86%, negative predictive value [NPV] 90.5%), outperforming preoperative RRI (AUROC 0.681). VExUS showed limited predictive performance (preoperative AUROC 0.588; postoperative AUROC 0.623). The baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) in the AKI group was significantly lower than in the patients who did not develop AKI [70.3 ml/min/1.73 m2 vs 79.4 ml/min/1.73 m2]. Diabetes mellitus was more common in the AKI group (62.5% vs 35.6%, P = 0.002). Postoperative urine output remained significantly lower in AKI patients on day 1 and day 2 (P < 0.001). Conclusion Postoperative RRI ≥ 0.68 demonstrated the best predictive performance for early AKI in our cohort, outperforming preoperative RRI, ΔRRI or change in RRI, and VExUS scores, supporting the predominant role of intrarenal arterial hemodynamic alterations in early postoperative renal injury.

title: Robotic Parenchyma-Preserving Pancreatic Resection for Focal Congenital Hyperinsulinism in an Infant.
abstract: Background Robot-assisted surgery has been increasingly adopted over traditional laparoscopic and open procedures. However, its application in neonates and infants remains limited. Restricted space, delicate tissues, and the need for special instruments complicate its use. This case report describes the application of robot-assisted surgery in an infant with focal congenital hyperinsulinism. Materials and methods We describe the management of focal congenital hyperinsulinism in an infant using robotic surgery with indocyanine green injection, intraoperative ultrasound, and a suture-based retraction technique. Case description Herein, we present a case of an infant weighing less than 5 kg who underwent robotic surgery. The procedure was performed using the 3 arms of the da Vinci Xi robotic system and a suture-based intraoperative retraction technique. Intraoperative frozen sections confirmed the complete excision of the focal disease. Final histopathology revealed focal adenomatous hyperplasia. Intraoperatively, plasma glucose levels transiently increased after resection peaking at 23.1 mmol/L. Intravenous dextrose was discontinued. The postoperative course was uneventful, and the infant was discharged on postoperative day nine after tolerating full oral feeds. At follow-up in 8 months, the child remained euglycemic without any medical therapy or hypoglycemic episodes. Discussion This case demonstrates the feasibility of robotic-assisted parenchyma-preserving pancreatic resection in a 4.6-kg infant. Careful attention to operative planning and the use of adjuncts, such as indocyanine green fluorescence and intraoperative ultrasonography, is critical. Minimizing the number of additional ports and using suture-based retraction techniques can help achieve successful robotic surgery in this high-risk population.

title: Deep Learning Trained Without Target-Domain Labels Improves Risk Stratification Over Expert Coronary Calcium Reading on Routine Attenuation Correction CT
abstract: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) is an established measure of coronary atherosclerosis on computed tomography (CT). Many SPECT and most PET myocardial perfusion studies already include a low-dose CT scan from which coronary calcium could be reported, yet it almost never is. CAC may not be reported due to image noise, cardiac motion, or the absence of a reliable reference standard. Deep learning (DL) models trained on these low-dose CT scans inherit the same uncertainty, because their reference labels are drawn on the degraded images. We bypassed this limitation by training a DL CAC model entirely outside the target domain: expert labels from high-quality gated CT were inherited by synthetic ungated images derived from those same scans, so that no CTAC scan was annotated, and no real CTAC image was used, at any point in training. Models were trained using one center and externally tested in two other centers. Because each synthetic image is derived from the gated scan itself, expert gated segmentations remain valid voxel-for-voxel without registration. Using these pairs, we developed a cross-domain knowledge adaptation model (knowledge adaptation, KAD-CAC). The DL models were externally tested on 5969 patients with a median age of 64 (IQR 56 - 73), of whom 50.2% were male. The KAD-CAC model had higher Cohens kappa K (0.86, 95% CI 0.84 - 0.88) compared to a convolutional LSTM model (K 0.78, 95% CI 0.76 - 0.80, p<0.01), or models trained with only gated images (K 0.81, 95% CI 0.80 - 0.82, p<0.01). Net reclassification improvement for death or myocardial infarction over a clinical and perfusion baseline was greatest for the KAD-CAC model and exceeded that of expert CAC reading on the same CTAC scans (difference 0.089, 95% CI 0.051 to 0.125, p<0.001). A model trained without any labels from CTAC scans therefore stratified risk of death or MI better than expert reading of the same scans. Patients classified as CAC 0 by KAD-CAC had lower adjusted risk of death or MI than patients classified as CAC 0 by experts (HR 0.50, 95% CI 0.25 - 0.98). We use paired synthetic ungated scans to transfer expert gated CAC annotations into the ungated domain, resulting in better vessel-level CAC scoring and improved risk reclassification compared with expert reading of the same scans. Automated CAC scoring could be added to every myocardial perfusion imaging report without additional imaging or radiation. The approach provides a general route to expert-quality supervision for any acquisition in which the native reference standard is unreliable.

title: Ascending Aortic Calcium Identifies Patients at Risk Despite Normal Myocardial Flow, Perfusion and Coronary Calcium: A 13-Site Cohort Study
abstract: Background Patients with normal perfusion, normal myocardial flow reserve (MFR) and no coronary artery calcium (CAC) on myocardial perfusion imaging are considered low risk. Yet, adverse events still occur and no routinely reported imaging marker stratifies residual risk. This study aims to determine whether fully automated ascending aortic calcification (AAC) from the attenuation correction CT stratifies risk in these patients. Methods In the multicenter REFINE-PET registry, AAC was quantified from non-contrast CT using deep learning aortic segmentation and Agatston scoring. Triple-normal was defined as stress total perfusion deficit (TPD) <5%, MFR >2 and CAC 0. The primary endpoint was cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or heart failure admission, with heart failure admission as key secondary endpoint. Cox models were adjusted for clinical confounders. Results Of 21,923 patients, 3,580 (16.3%) were triple-normal, of whom 1,322 (36.9%) had AAC (median Agatston 65, IQR 22-212). Agreement with three blinded readers was good to excellent (Intraclass correlation coefficient 0.87-0.90). Over a median follow-up of 52 months (IQR 26-69), 194 primary events occurred. Per standard deviation, AAC was independently associated with the primary endpoint (adjusted HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.09-1.40; p<0.001), heart failure admission (adjusted HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.10-1.55; p=0.003) and all-cause mortality (adjusted HR 1.17, 95% CI 1.04-1.32; p=0.009). AAC improved model fit beyond clinical factors, MFR and TPD (p≤0.009), with modest gains in discrimination (ΔC 0.007-0.009). Conclusions In patients with normal PET readouts, automated AAC was independently associated with adverse outcomes, most strongly heart failure admission, beyond clinical risk factors, perfusion and flow. Clinical Perspective What Is New? In 3,580 patients with normal perfusion, normal myocardial flow reserve and no coronary artery calcium on PET, more than one in three had ascending aortic calcification on the attenuation correction CT. Ascending aortic calcification was independently associated with cardiovascular death, myocardial infarction or heart failure admission (adjusted hazard ratio per SD 1.24, 95% CI 1.09-1.40), most strongly with heart failure admission. A fast, fully automated method scored ascending aortic calcification with agreement to expert readers similar to agreement between readers. What Are the Clinical Implications? A normal perfusion PET with normal flow and no coronary calcium does not mean uniformly low risk when the ascending aorta is calcified. Because ascending aortic calcification is scored automatically from the CT acquired with every perfusion PET, it could be reported routinely without additional scanning, cost or radiation. Patients presumed low risk who have ascending aortic calcification may warrant heart failure-oriented prevention, such as natriuretic peptide screening, pending prospective validation.

abstract: ABSTRACT Traumatic brain injury (TBI) initiates secondary neurodegeneration that compromises interconnected neural circuits and contributes to persistent visual and neurobehavioral impairment. Pharmacological strategies that preserve vulnerable neurons and synapses while limiting chronic neuroinflammation remain an unmet therapeutic need. We previously identified the serotonin 1A receptor (5-HT1A) antagonist WAY-100635 through screening human stem cell-derived retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and demonstrated that it promotes neuroprotection through cyclic adenosine monophosphate-dependent mitochondrial biogenesis. Here, we investigated whether post-injury treatment extends this neuroprotective efficacy to cerebral and visual circuitry following TBI. Male C57BL/6J mice aged 2-3 months underwent unilateral controlled cortical impact (CCI) involving the left visual cortex. Mice were randomly assigned to sham, untreated injury or treated injury groups, with 3-10 sham controls and 5-8 mice per injury group across experiments. WAY-100635 was administered intraperitoneally at 5 mg/kg daily, beginning 1 hour after injury and continuing for 6 weeks. Therapeutic efficacy was assessed using motor and psychological-health-relevant risk-taking/behavioral disinhibition by elevated-plus-maze assessment, visual electrophysiology, optokinetic responses, diffusion magnetic resonance imaging, and retinal and cortical histopathology. Unilateral cortical injury produced bilateral RGC dysfunction and loss, with greater degeneration in the eye contralateral to the injured hemisphere, consistent with predominantly crossed murine visual projections. WAY-100635 significantly preserved RGC survival and function, improved visual acuity and contrast sensitivity, and preserved visually evoked cortical responses to contralateral eye stimulation. Diffusion MRI revealed bilateral visual pathway abnormalities, with treatment selectively normalizing fractional anisotropy and radial kurtosis in the optic tract ipsilateral to cortical injury. In perilesional cortex, treatment preserved neuronal cell bodies and synapses detected by synaptophysin immunoreactivity while markedly reducing microglial/macrophage activation and reactive astrogliosis. These effects were accompanied by improved early motor performance and attenuation of injury-associated increases in open-arm exploration in the elevated plus maze. Cortical cavity volume was not significantly reduced, supporting preferential protection of vulnerable circuitry surrounding and connected to the primary lesion. These findings identify post-injury WAY-100635 treatment as a novel therapeutic intervention that combines neuronal and synaptic preservation with reduced chronic glial activation and improved functional outcomes. They support further translational development of serotonin 1A receptor antagonism to limit secondary neurodegeneration and the visual and neurobehavioral consequences of TBI. Graphical Abstract

title: BaT-SAM: Introducing Inductive Bias into SAM via a Mixture of Convolutional Experts for Brain Tumor Segmentation
abstract: Accurate brain tumor segmentation from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is essential for diagnosis and treatment planning; however, manual delineation is labor-intensive and time-consuming. Existing approaches are either task-specific with limited generalization or rely on user-provided prompts during inference. We present BaT-SAM, a parameter-efficient adaptation framework that enables fully automatic brain tumor segmentation with the Segment Anything Model (SAM). BaT-SAM injects local inductive bias into SAM's frozen Vision Transformer (ViT) encoder via Conv-LoRA, where image features are processed by a sparsely gated mixture of multi-scale convolutional experts. This design compensates for the limited translation-equivariant inductive bias of vanilla ViTs while fine-tuning fewer than 5M parameters (less than 1% of the full model). To remove the need for user prompts, we further introduce a lightweight self-prompting box regressor that is jointly optimized with the adapter using scheduled sampling and predicts tumor locations directly from image embeddings. On the BRISC2025 benchmark, BaT-SAM achieves a weighted mean IoU of 0.832 while outperforming state-of-the-art benchmarks. It further demonstrates strong cross-dataset generalization, achieving Dice scores of 0.702 on Figshare and 0.784 on the LGG MRI Segmentation dataset.

title: Lesion-Aware Attention for Mammography Segmentation with Heterogeneous Supervision
abstract: Accurate lesion segmentation in mammography is important for computer-aided breast cancer diagnosis, but dense pixel-level annotations remain costly and limited. Existing public segmentation datasets usually cover only a small set of lesion types with manually delineated masks, whereas larger mammography datasets often provide only image-level diagnostic labels. This annotation mismatch makes it difficult to train segmentation models that can generalize to rare or weakly annotated lesion categories. To address this problem, we study open-vocabulary mammographic lesion segmentation under a mixed-supervision setting, where pixel-level masks are available for base lesion categories and image-level labels are available for a broader set of categories. We propose a two-branch framework that jointly learns from segmentation data and classification data. The segmentation branch learns lesion boundaries from annotated masks, while the classification branch introduces additional image-level semantic supervision. To better transfer image-level supervision to lesion-relevant regions, we further introduce a Lesion-wise Attentive Classifier that maintains category-specific feature prototypes and generates lesion-aware attention maps for foreground feature pooling. This design reduces the influence of background tissue and encourages more compact lesion representations. Experiments on multiple mammography datasets show that the proposed method consistently improves open-vocabulary segmentation baselines on both base and novel lesion categories, while reducing the gap to fully supervised models that require dense target-domain masks. Qualitative results further indicate that our method produces more complete lesion localization for small, low-contrast, and visually subtle mammographic findings.

title: Generalizable fetal brain biometry via adaptive artificial intelligence
abstract: Reliable fetal brain biometry on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is essential for diagnosing congenital brain anomalies, but artificial intelligence models often lose accuracy under domain shifts. We developed BioTTA, a backbone-agnostic, source-free unsupervised test-time adaptation framework that adapts pretrained models online to individual unlabeled target volumes. This retrospective multicohort study included 394 reconstructed 3D fetal brain MRI volumes at 20-39 gestational weeks, with 11 biometric measurements annotated by radiologists. BioTTA was developed on single-center turbo spin-echo MRI and evaluated on three datasets representing cross-sequence, cross-center, and cross-nation shifts. Biometry accuracy was assessed using mean absolute error (MAE) and the percentage of correct measurements within 4 mm. A web-based reporting platform mapped measurements onto normative growth trajectories and was evaluated against radiologists in four multicenter disease cohorts covering germinal matrix-intraventricular hemorrhage, ventriculomegaly, and cerebellar abnormality. Across all three target datasets, BioTTA outperformed auto-SVRTK, source-only models, and FetalSynthGen, while matching models finetuned with target labels. MAEs ranged from 1.10 to 1.46 mm with a convolutional backbone and from 1.46 to 2.25 mm with a transformer backbone. Diagnostic accuracy ranged from 82.1% to 95.0%, comparable to a senior radiologist. BioTTA supports accurate, generalizable fetal brain biometry and standardized prenatal brain growth assessment across heterogeneous MRI sources.

title: Editorial Commentary: Hip Microinstability: Stability Is the Goal, Plication Is a Tool.
abstract: Hip microinstability remains one of the most challenging conditions we encounter in hip preservation surgery. The difficulty is not performing a capsular plication but determining when instability is truly present and clinically relevant. In our experience, no single clinical, radiographic, or intraoperative finding should define the diagnosis. Rather, the entire clinical picture must be considered when evaluating the potentially unstable hip. Capsular plication represents an important component of this strategy but should not be considered in isolation. Careful diagnosis and thoughtful patient selection remain fundamental to successful treatment of hip microinstability.

title: Nanoprobe-Enabled Precision Imaging and Panoramic Boundary Delineation in Retinoblastoma.
abstract: Retinoblastoma is the most common primary intraocular malignancy in children. Its prognosis depends critically on accurate delineation of the tumor and its margins, early detection of small lesions, and timely monitoring of therapeutic response. Traditional single-modality imaging techniques are inherently constrained by trade-offs among spatial resolution, molecular sensitivity, and dynamic imaging capability, making them insufficient for the demands of precision diagnosis and treatment. In recent years, nanomedicine-based imaging strategies have emerged as promising approaches to overcome these limitations. Through rational design of nanoprobes with tunable physicochemical properties, active targeting capabilities, and integrated multimodal signaling, researchers have achieved more comprehensive visualization and diagnostic evaluation of retinoblastoma lesions. In this review, we systematically summarize the major imaging modalities applied to retinoblastoma, including optical imaging, ultrasound (US), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and photoacoustic imaging (PAI). Subsequently, the corresponding imaging probes and targeting strategies were discussed, which were developed to enhance the imaging contrast and improve the spatiotemporal resolution of tumor visualization. Furthermore, we highlight the emerging role of artificial intelligence (AI) in the rational design of high-performance imaging nanoprobes and in multimodal image analysis, emphasizing its potential to enable quantitative tumor and boundary delineation. Finally, we outline the key challenges that must be addressed to advance the clinical translation of nanoprobes, including the identification of novel targeting strategies, AI-assisted image analysis, the development of models that more accurately recapitulate the human ocular microenvironment, and the application of new biocompatible materials. Overall, this review aims to provide comprehensive and insightful guidance for the development of next-generation nanoprobes for the precise visualization and boundary delineation of retinoblastoma.

title: Intraoperative Application of the PRAETORIAN Score to Predict Optimal Subcutaneous Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator Placement.
abstract: Background The PRAETORIAN score (PS) estimates the risk of defibrillation failure after subcutaneous implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (S-ICD) implantation based on postoperative chest radiography in the standing position. However, the usefulness of assessing the PS in the supine position intraoperatively has not yet been established. Methods We evaluated conventional (standing) and intraoperative supine PS in 124 consecutive Japanese patients undergoing S-ICD implantation. Changes between conventional and supine PS values were analyzed in two ways: (1) the presence of any difference in the absolute PS values regardless of the risk category, and (2) changes in clinically relevant risk categories for conversion failure (low, intermediate, or high risk). Predictors of discordance between the two assessments were also investigated. Results The median conventional PS was 30; 116 and 8 patients were classified as having low and intermediate risk of conversion failure, respectively. Numerical differences between the conventional and supine PS values were observed in 13 patients. However, clinically meaningful risk reclassification occurred in only two patients, suggesting that intraoperative supine PS assessment may underestimate PRAETORIAN score-based risk classification in a small subset of patients. Among patients with numerical PS changes, supine PS was significantly lower than conventional PS. An elevated BMI was strongly associated with PS discordance. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic curve analysis identified a BMI cutoff of 25.6 kg/m 2 for discriminating patients with numerical PS discordance. Conclusions Intraoperative supine PS assessment shows excellent concordance with conventional standing PS and may provide a practical tool for confirming appropriate system positioning in most Japanese patients.

title: Transformer-Based Preoperative Invasiveness Identification and Postoperative Recurrence Risk Stratification in Stage T1N0M0 Lung Adenocarcinoma: A Multi-Center Cohort Study.
abstract: Surgery is the primary curative treatment for early-stage lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), with accurate identification of tumor invasiveness critical for determining pulmonary resection extent. Due to significant variability in postoperative recurrence among early-stage LUAD patients with aggressive tumors, a more effective risk stratification system is urgently needed to improve prognosis. This study developed the T1LUT system, a transformer-based tool for T1N0M0 LUAD management, covering preoperative tumor invasiveness identification and postoperative recurrence risk stratification. Preoperatively, a 3D Vision Transformer (ViT) with extra learnable tokens analyzes CT images. It outperforms 3D ViT with only CLS tokens, 2D ViT, and 3D ResNet across three independent test centers (Center D: 0.896 vs. 0.892, 0.879, 0.836; Center E: 0.906 vs. 0.837, 0.837, 0.835; Center F: 0.884 vs. 0.884, 0.881, 0.861), achieving higher mean AUROC to accurately assess invasiveness and guide surgical resection extent. Postoperatively, the multimodal IAC-PR model integrates CT images, reports, pathological data, and clinical/demographic information. It stratifies invasive adenocarcinoma (IAC) patients into low-, medium-, or high-risk groups with an AUROC of 0.807 in testing-significantly better than single/partial-modal models. Validated via large-scale multicenter research, this system overcomes traditional assessment limitations, offering a robust tool for precise early LUAD treatment and improved prognosis.

title: External root resorption prevalence on adjacent teeth associated with maxillary impacted canines in CBCT images.
abstract: Purpose External root resorption (ERR) is a significant complication associated with impacted maxillary canines that can affect the prognosis of adjacent teeth. This study evaluated the prevalence, anatomical distribution, and risk factors of ERR in teeth adjacent to impacted maxillary canines using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT). Methods This retrospective cross-sectional study analyzed CBCT images of 66 patients (81 impacted canines) with maxillary canine impaction. An endodontist and radiologist evaluated impaction characteristics, proximity relationships (≤ 0.5 mm), and ERR presence, location, and severity in adjacent teeth using consensus-based assessment. Results ERR was detected in 50 of 243 adjacent teeth (20.58%). Lateral incisors showed significantly higher resorption prevalence (35.80%) compared to central incisors (13.58%) and first premolars (11.11%) (p < 0.001). Physical proximity was strongly associated with resorption occurrence across all tooth types (p < 0.001). Buccal canine positioning significantly increased central incisor resorption risk (p = 0.019). Heat map analysis revealed middle third predominance in central incisors, while lateral incisors showed more distributed patterns between middle and apical thirds. Root development stage and follicle width showed no significant associations with resorption presence. Conclusion Physical proximity emerges as the primary determinant of ERR risk in teeth adjacent to impacted maxillary canines. Lateral incisors demonstrate the highest vulnerability, while the buccal positioning of the canine tooth specifically increases central incisor resorption risk. CBCT evaluation with detailed anatomical assessment is essential for comprehensive risk evaluation and treatment planning in maxillary canine impaction cases.

title: Evaluation of PET-detected nodal upstaging and planning target volume expansion in esophageal cancer radiotherapy planning.
abstract: Background While 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography (FDG-PET/CT) is known to influence staging, its quantitative impact on clinically meaningful target volume expansion remains incompletely characterized. We evaluated whether PET-detected nodal upstaging is associated with significant planning target volume (PTV) expansion. Methods Fifty consecutive eligible patients with esophageal cancer undergoing computed tomography (CT)- and PET-based radiotherapy planning between January 2018 and January 2022 were retrospectively analyzed, with no predefined target sample size. Clinically significant PTV expansion was predefined as a > 10% increase from CT-based to PET-based planning. Associations between PET-detected nodal upstaging and PTV expansion were evaluated using Fisher's exact test, logistic regression, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and nonparametric testing. Given the limited number of events, a parsimonious multivariable model and threshold sensitivity analyses were additionally performed. Results Patients with nodal upstaging had a significantly higher risk of > 10% PTV expansion (48.0% vs. 16.7%; absolute risk difference 31.3%, 95% CI 6.7-55.9%; p = 0.032). The median percent PTV change was significantly higher in patients with nodal upstaging (9.49% vs. 0.31%; Wilcoxon p < 0.001). In a parsimonious multivariable model adjusting for tumor length, nodal upstaging remained independently associated with clinically significant PTV expansion (odds ratio (OR) 4.38, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.12-17.10; p = 0.033). Model discrimination was acceptable (area under the curve (AUC) 0.7254), with stable performance on bootstrap internal validation (bootstrap mean AUC 0.733). Sensitivity analyses using alternative expansion thresholds (> 5%, > 10%, and > 15%) demonstrated directionally consistent associations. Patients meeting the PTV expansion threshold also demonstrated significantly greater increases in lung dose-volume burden (mean lung dose, and lung volumes receiving 5 Gy and 20 Gy; all p < 0.001) in paired dosimetric comparison, supporting the clinical relevance of this threshold. Conclusion During esophageal cancer radiotherapy planning, PET-detected nodal upstaging was independently associated with clinically meaningful target volume expansion. The association was consistent across alternative expansion thresholds and in bootstrap internal validation, and a paired lung dose-volume comparison indicated that the expansion threshold corresponds to a measurable increase in lung dose burden.

title: [Enteral contrast agents-When, what and how?]
abstract: Background Administration of enteral contrast media (CM) in abdominal computed tomography (CT) is handled inconsistently across Germany. Objective To present the current recommendations on administration of enteral contrast agents along the guiding questions of when, what and how and to translate them into radiological practice. Material and methods Synthesis of indication-based recommendations, CM classes and their technical properties and the practical execution of both routes of administration, based on the recommendations of the German Röntgen Society (DRG), current guidelines, published evidence and institutional practice. Results Positive oral CMs are obsolete for most abdominal indications, including acute abdomen, ileus and trauma, and are contraindicated when gastrointestinal bleeding or ischemia is suspected. In cases of suspected perforation, routine oral contrast agents should be omitted and barium sulphate is contraindicated, whereas water-soluble iodinated agents remain an option when a leak has to be specifically demonstrated. Furthermore, enteral contrasting with neutral oral CM remains useful for upper gastrointestinal tumor staging and enterography (preferably magnetic resonance enterography). Conclusion An indication-appropriate, guideline-based enteral contrast agent administration reduces unnecessary burden without compromising diagnostic accuracy and should be embedded in standardized workflows.

title: Deep learning super-resolution enhances MRI radiomics for predicting placenta accreta spectrum and invasiveness.
abstract: Objectives Placenta Accreta Spectrum (PAS) is a severe obstetric complication. This study evaluated whether retrospective, post-processing deep learning-based super-resolution reconstruction (SR) was associated with improved MRI radiomics performance for predicting PAS and invasive PAS. Materials & methods This retrospective study involved 245 patients who had placental MRI scans at three different institutions. Of these, 158 cases from Institution I for training set and internal validation set, while 34 patients from Institution II and 53 patients from Institution III served as external validation sets. SR using a generative adversarial network (GAN) was applied to generate SR T2WI (SRT2WI). Predictive models for PAS and invasive PAS were developed based on T2WI, SRT2WI, and the SRT2WI-Clinical model. Two radiologists independently diagnosed PAS using T2WI to serve as a reference for evaluating model performance. Model performance was assessed using the area under the curve (AUC), calibration curves, decision curve analysis (DCA), Delong test, and net reclassification improvement (NRI). SHAP values interpreted the models and quantified feature contributions. Results Across all four cohorts, SRT2WI yielded numerically higher AUCs than T2WI, and SRT2WI-Clinical achieved the highest AUCs. For PAS, SRT2WI-Clinical achieved AUCs of 0.953, 0.887, 0.793, and 0.788 in the training, internal validation, and external validation cohorts 1 and 2, respectively (T2WI: 0.738, 0.697, 0.654, and 0.652; SRT2WI: 0.879, 0.820, 0.696, and 0.768). Corresponding AUCs for invasive PAS were 0.895, 0.875, 0.843, and 0.815 (T2WI: 0.774, 0.699, 0.575, and 0.745; SRT2WI: 0.861, 0.794, 0.729, and 0.808). For PAS, SRT2WI-Clinical significantly outperformed T2WI (P < 0.001) and SRT2WI (P = 0.004) only in training, with no significant validation differences. For invasive PAS, it significantly outperformed T2WI in training, internal validation, and external validation cohort 1 (P = 0.003, 0.021, and 0.019, respectively), but not external validation cohort 2 (P = 0.398); comparisons with SRT2WI were nonsignificant. Calibration showed good agreement, DCA favored SRT2WI-Clinical, and SHAP quantified feature contributions. Conclusions The combination of SR and radiomics shows promise for improving the prediction of PAS and invasive PAS. Integrating clinical features may further enhance model performance, supporting its potential clinical utility.

title: Automated segmentation-based emergency CT radiomics for predicting functional outcome at discharge and in-hospital post-stroke pneumonia in primary brainstem hemorrhage.
abstract: Background Primary brainstem hemorrhage (PBSH) is associated with high mortality, disability, and uncertain early outcomes. Emergency non-contrast CT (NCCT) is the earliest imaging examination, but conventional assessment may not fully capture hematoma heterogeneity. This study aimed to develop an automated segmentation-based emergency NCCT radiomics framework for predicting poor functional outcome at discharge and in-hospital post-stroke pneumonia (PSP) in PBSH. Methods This retrospective study included 372 patients with PBSH, comprising a training set (n = 182), an internal test set (n = 79), and a temporal internal validation set (n = 111). Hematomas were segmented using a three-dimensional U-Net. Manual and automated segmentation-based radiomics models were compared, and automated segmentation-derived radiomics features were integrated with conventional radiological predictors to construct combined models for poor functional outcome and PSP. Results The automated segmentation-based radiomics model showed comparable performance to the manual segmentation-based model across all three datasets. The combined prognostic model achieved AUCs of 0.926, 0.923, and 0.858 in the training, internal test, and temporal internal validation sets, with higher AUCs and lower Brier scores than the conventional radiological model. The combined PSP model (AUCs: 0.828, 0.742, 0.681) showed no consistent improvement. SHAP identified hematoma classification as the most influential prognostic predictor. Conclusions Automated segmentation-based NCCT radiomics is feasible for early risk stratification in PBSH. The combined prognostic model showed good discrimination and potential complementary value beyond conventional CT assessment. The PSP model remains exploratory and requires further refinement and validation.

This study aimed to develop an automated segmentation-based emergency NCCT radiomics framework for predicting poor functional outcome at discharge and in-hospital post-stroke pneumonia (PSP) in PBSH.

Methods

This retrospective study included 372 patients with PBSH, comprising a training set (n = 182), an internal test set (n = 79), and a temporal internal validation set (n = 111). Hematomas were segmented using a three-dimensional U-Net. Manual and automated segmentation-based radiomics models were compared, and automated segmentation-derived radiomics features were integrated with conventional radiological predictors to construct combined models for poor functional outcome and PSP.

Results

The automated segmentation-based radiomics model showed comparable performance to the manual segmentation-based model across all three datasets. The combined prognostic model achieved AUCs of 0.926, 0.923, and 0.858 in the training, internal test, and temporal internal validation sets, with higher AUCs and lower Brier scores than the conventional radiological model. The combined PSP model (AUCs: 0.828, 0.742, 0.681) showed no consistent improvement. SHAP identified hematoma classification as the most influential prognostic predictor.

Conclusions

Automated segmentation-based NCCT radiomics is feasible for early risk stratification in PBSH. The combined prognostic model showed good discrimination and potential complementary value beyond conventional CT assessment. The PSP model remains exploratory and requires further refinement and validation.

title: Pelvic splenosis and endometriosis in adolescent with hereditary spherocytosis.
abstract: The patient is a 16-year-old with a history of hereditary spherocytosis. At age 12, she underwent a laparoscopic partial converted to total splenectomy for intraoperative bleeding. The spleen was placed in a retrieval bag and removed via morcellation. She first reported abdominal pain at age 8, with dysmenorrhea after menarche at age 13. Her dysmenorrhea was managed with a progesterone IUD. Due to worsening pain, she underwent MRI which showed multiple lobulated structures throughout the pelvis and ventral abdomen, suggestive of endometriomas versus splenules. Laparoscopy revealed dozens of black-blue nodules coating the anterior abdominal wall and multiple multi-centimeter nodules attached to the sigmoid colon, descending colon, jejunum, and ovarian fossae, with vesicular lesions deep in pelvis. Abdominal wall and pelvic lesions were excised; removal of the nodules adherent to the colon and small bowel was deferred given inadequate bowel preparation. Frozen section and final histopathology confirmed splenosis throughout the abdomen and pelvis, with presence of endometriosis in right uterosacral ligament and ovarian fossa. Future surgery is planned to excise remaining splenules. This patient's case demonstrates that splenosis and endometriosis can exist simultaneously and are difficult to differentiate from one another symptomatically, on imaging, and even under direct visualization. Gynecologic surgeons should include splenosis in the differential diagnosis of pelvic nodular masses, particularly in patients with a history of splenectomy.

title: Three-Year Follow-Up of Clinical, Radiographic, and Patient-Reported Outcomes for Zirconia and Titanium Implants in the Posterior Region: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
abstract: Objective To compare the 3-year clinical, radiographic, esthetic, and patient-reported outcomes of zirconia (Zr) and titanium (Ti) implants placed in posterior sites in a randomized, controlled within-subject design. Materials and methods Forty-two patients each received one Zr and one Ti implant. Clinical and radiographic outcomes were evaluated at baseline, 1, and 3 years after crown delivery. Marginal bone levels (MBL), peri-implant soft-tissue parameters, technical complications, esthetic outcomes (ΔE values, VAS scores), and patient-reported measures were assessed. Thirty-nine patients (37 Zr; 39 Ti implants) were available at 3 years. Results The 3-year survival rate was 100% for Ti and 94.9% for Zr implants. MBL remained stable after the initial remodeling phase, with no clinically relevant differences between materials. Peri-implant soft-tissue conditions (BOP, plaque presence, PD, KT) were similar for Zr and Ti. Two zirconia implants were lost during the observation period. Peri-implantitis was diagnosed in 7.9% of the implants, affecting three titanium and three zirconia implants. Technical complications differed between groups: chipping occurred significantly more often at Zr implant-supported crowns. Ti implants showed two screw-loosening events, while Zr implants showed two cases of decementation. Esthetic and patient-reported outcomes were comparable, with low perceived mucosal color differences and a slight preference for Zr sites, if detectable. Conclusion Zr and Ti implants showed similar peri-implant health, marginal bone stability, esthetic outcomes, and patient satisfaction after 3 years. Zr implants, however, demonstrated a slightly lower survival rate and more chipping. Trial registration The trial is registered in the German Clinical Trials Register (DRKS) under the ID DRKS00008591.

title: Predictive Value of Preoperative Examinations for Early Prognosis After Functional Endoscopic Sinus Surgery in Chronic Rhinosinusitis With Nasal Polyps.
abstract: Background Functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS) remains a primary treatment modality for chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) refractory to medical management. This study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of routine preoperative examinations for early surgical outcomes following FESS in patients with CRSwNP. Methods This prospective cohort study evaluated whether routine preoperative assessments predict early outcomes after FESS in 181 patients with bilateral CRSwNP. Preoperative evaluations included Lund-Mackay CT scores, Lund-Kennedy endoscopy scores, symptom Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), SNOT-22 and peripheral blood eosinophil counts. Patients were followed postoperatively at 2 weeks, 1, 3 and 6 months. Results Preoperative VAS showed the strongest correlation with 2-week symptom improvement (r = 0.633), remaining an independent predictor in multivariate analysis (β = 0.58). Preoperative SNOT-22 also independently predicted 2-week outcomes (β = 0.15). At 3 months, blood eosinophil counts predicted endoscopic improvement (r = 0.305), while preoperative Lund-Kennedy scores strongly predicted 6-month endoscopic outcomes (r = 0.508). Conclusions Routine preoperative assessments provide valuable predictive information for early postoperative outcomes following FESS in CRSwNP. We expect these findings to support the integration of multimodal preoperative assessment to guide patient counselling and postoperative management expectations.

title: Catecholamine-Secreting Retroperitoneal Paraganglioma: A Case Report and Literature Review.
abstract: Introduction Paragangliomas are rare neuroendocrine tumors arising from autonomic paraganglia. These tumors have metastatic potential, and histopathological findings alone cannot reliably predict their biological behavior. Clinical manifestations range from the classic triad of headache, diaphoresis, and palpitations to incidental findings in asymptomatic patients. Case presentation A 75-year-old man was incidentally found to have a 5 cm retroperitoneal mass adjacent to the right renal hilum. Biochemical testing confirmed marked catecholamine hypersecretion, and 18F-FDOPA PET/CT demonstrated isolated uptake within the lesion without additional disease. Preoperative preparation included progressive alpha-adrenergic blockade with doxazosin for approximately 1 month, followed by atenolol for heart rate control. An open approach through a right subcostal hemichevron incision was selected because the tumor was located between the right renal artery and vein and lateral to the inferior vena cava. During dissection, an iatrogenic renal artery injury with intraoperative hemorrhage occurred, necessitating en bloc removal of the tumor, right kidney, and right adrenal gland. Histopathological examination confirmed a paraganglioma with a Ki-67 proliferation index below 1%, focal nuclear atypia, no mitotic figures, no tumor necrosis, no vascular invasion, and microscopic margin involvement. Immunohistochemistry was positive for Chromogranin A, synaptophysin, GATA-3, and S100. Germline testing using a 14-gene pheochromocytoma-paraganglioma panel identified no reported pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants. At 6 months, contrast-enhanced thoracoabdominopelvic computed tomography showed no evidence of local recurrence or metastatic disease, and plasma and urinary metanephrines had normalized, consistent with postoperative biochemical remission. The patient remains under joint endocrinology and urology follow-up with lifelong annual clinical and biochemical surveillance. Discussion and conclusion This case highlights the diagnostic and surgical challenges of a functioning perihilar retroperitoneal paraganglioma. Careful endocrine preparation, vascular planning, multidisciplinary management, and lifelong surveillance are essential, particularly when the surgical margin is microscopically involved.

title: Pleuroparenchymal fibroelastosis in a monogenic mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome.
abstract: Background Pleuroparenchymal fibroelastosis (PPFE) is a rare, most often idiopathic fibrotic lung disease with poor prognosis, mainly affecting adults. Biallelic pathogenic variants in the deoxyguanosine kinase gene ( DGUOK ) cause a mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) depletion syndrome, predominantly affecting infants with severe hepatic and neurological disease. Neither detailed pulmonary manifestations nor a pulmonary-dominant phenotype has been reported. Methods We describe nine patients with PPFE and DGUOK -associated mitochondriopathy. Clinical, radiological, histopathological, and genetic data were systematically collected from all patients. Functional studies, single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNAseq), immunofluorescence staining, transmission electron microscopy, respiratory chain enzyme activity assays and mtDNA recovery experiment were conducted on patient-derived fibroblasts, muscle or lung tissues. mtDNA content quantification was performed on whole genome sequencing data. Results All patients (ages 5-36 years) carried biallelic pathogenic DGUOK variants, including an unreported intronic alteration in seven. All presented with progressive dyspnea, weight loss and some with pneumothoraces. Chest computed tomography and lung biopsies demonstrated features of PPFE. snRNAseq of lung tissue from four pediatric patients identified Aberrant Basaloid cells at the fibrotic edge, together with a transcriptional signature of nuclear DNA damage response. Ultrastructural analysis confirmed mitochondrial abnormalities in alveolar type 2 and Aberrant Basaloid cells. Conclusion This study provides evidence that mitochondrial dysfunction can contribute to early-onset PPFE independent of age, with a DNA damage response signature in aberrant epithelial cell populations previously described only in adult fibrotic lung disease. DGUOK deficiency and other hereditary mitochondrial disorders should be considered in children and young adults presenting with PPFE of unknown origin.

title: Transcutaneous Skin Perforation by a Protruding Xiphoid Process in a Bedbound Patient With Post-Traumatic Cervical Myelopathy: A Case Report and Review of the Literature
abstract: Abstract Background The xiphoid process is the smallest and most morphologically variable component of the sternum, and anterior (ventral) deviation is a recognized anatomical variant. Symptomatic xiphoid disease typically presents as localized pain (xiphodynia). Cutaneous complications are exceedingly uncommon, and only a single previous report describing an ischemic xiphisternal ulcer associated with a protruding xiphoid has been published. To the best of our knowledge, we identified no previous English-language report describing complete transcutaneous perforation of the skin by a protruding xiphoid process associated with chronic sinus formation and secondary infection. Case presentation A 71-year-old bedbound man with type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and post-traumatic cervical myelopathy with spastic weakness developed progressive protrusion of the xiphoid process. The angulated xiphoid tip gradually eroded through the overlying skin, producing a chronic midline ulcer with sinus tract formation and superimposed infection. Lateral radiography demonstrated marked anterior angulation of the xiphoid process with prominent ventral protrusion and irregularity of the distal tip. The patient underwent xiphoidectomy with en-bloc excision of the ulcer and debridement of devitalized soft tissue. Intraoperative culture of the resected xiphoid specimen yielded extended-spectrum beta-lactamase (ESBL)-producing Escherichia coli, and culture-directed carbapenem therapy was administered. Histopathological examination revealed extensive ulceration with inflamed granulation tissue and a sinus tract, accompanied by reactive squamous epithelial hyperplasia (pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia), whereas the underlying bone was unremarkable and showed no evidence of malignancy. Conclusions A protruding xiphoid process can rarely progress beyond pain and superficial ulceration to cutaneous breach with sinus tract formation and secondary infection, particularly in debilitated patients with chronic immobility, diabetes mellitus, and reduced soft-tissue padding. This process appears mechanistically analogous to a pressure ulcer developing over an atypical bony prominence. Xiphoidectomy combined with debridement and culture-directed antimicrobial therapy appears to provide definitive treatment. Histopathological examination is essential because reactive pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia at the ulcer margin may mimic cutaneous malignancy.

title: Cephalothoracoomphalopagus Tetrabrachius Tetrapus Conjoined Twins: An Extremely Rare Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Conjoined twins are a rare subset of monozygotic twins that usually have a poor prognosis, which has become a significant cause of perinatal morbidity and mortality. This case highlights the importance of routine antenatal care for earlier prenatal diagnosis and well-informed family counseling concerning appropriate intervention for conjoined twins. Case presentation: A 31-year-old G2P1 female in 29 4/7 weeks of gestation was referred from a primary health care center to our hospital with conjoined twins. Two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) ultrasonography examinations at 29 4/7 weeks of gestation revealed one fetal head accompanied by an orbital hypotelorism with an interocular diameter of 0.99 cm. The liver and heart were found to be the fusion organs involved. Polyhydramnios was observed with a maximum vertical pocket of 12.07 cm. Diagnosis of cephalo-thoraco-omphalopagus conjoined twins was made right after the first scan and consistently confirmed thereafter by six more repeated ultrasound examinations. Clinical examination after scheduled surgical delivery in 33 5/7 weeks old neonates revealed male conjoined twins with a fused head accompanied by two pairs of ears, along with a single trunk together with four neurologically independent upper limbs and lower limbs, as well as two complements of genitalia and two anuses. The twin showed signs of respiratory distress and died within one hour of birth. Conclusion Routine antenatal care and advanced ultrasound scanning are crucial for earlier prenatal diagnosis and well-informed family counseling concerning appropriate intervention for conjoined twins.

title: A novel sub-junctional pinhole technique (S-PHT) in treating intrabony defects of stage III periodontitis – Case Series
abstract: Abstract Background Sub-junctional pinhole technique (S-PHT) is a minimally invasive approach in which graft material is introduced into the intrabony defect through a pinhole made on the facial surface opposite to the intrabony defect alveolar crest and apical to the junctional epithelium 4 weeks following minimally invasive non-surgical therapy. This strategy is intended to keep the long junctional epithelium as a biologic seal over the grafted material, while providing maximum soft tissue support around the grafted material. Methods This case series presents the short-term outcome of ten patients diagnosed with stage III grade A periodontitis with interproximal intrabony defects of at least 3 mm, treated with S-PHT. Xenogenic graft material was introduced into the defect through a facial pinhole opposite to the alveolar crest following defect degranulation using minimally invasive hand and ultrasonic instrumentation. Clinical and radiographic parameters were recorded at baseline (4 weeks after non-surgical therapy) and at 9 months following S-PHT. Results Nine months following S-PHT, all sites measured ≤ 4mm probing pocket depth (PPD). The number of sites with clinical attachment level (CAL) gain ≥ 3mm was 6 out of the 10 reported cases. Six sites out of the 10 cases fulfilled a composite outcome of pocket closure of ≤ 4 mm with ≥ 3 mm attachment gain and no bleeding on probing. Significant improvement in intrabony defect fill reported after 9 months with a mean defect fill of 3.1 mm (< 0.001). Conclusions This case series demonstrates that S-PHT, as a minimally invasive approach, could be a reliable patient friendly option for treating intrabony defects in stage III periodontitis. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov. identifiers NCT07763223 PRT-RCT-2026-001 (05-08-2026 and retrospectively registered 19-08-2026)

title: A Decade-Old Retained Intrapleural Glass Fragment in an Asymptomatic Skydiver: A Case Report and Review of the Literature
abstract: Abstract Retained intrathoracic foreign bodies are usually discovered after a traumatic event that the patient clearly remembers. Glass, however, can be especially problematic. It is frequently retained, may be missed during the initial assessment, can appear variably on imaging, and may migrate months or even years after injury rather than becoming securely encapsulated. To our knowledge, an entirely asymptomatic intrapleural glass fragment discovered incidentally in a skydiver has not previously been reported. We describe a 34-year-old male skydiver who was referred after a routine screening chest radiograph showed an abnormal shadow in the right hemithorax. Ten years earlier, he had sustained a penetrating right-sided chest injury during a parachute landing, when he crashed through a window. At that time, he was treated for haemopneumothorax with intercostal drainage, but no foreign body was suspected or actively sought. On current examination, he had a contracted right hemithorax. Computed tomography revealed a radio-dense pleural foreign body. Right-sided thoracotomy was performed, and a 7 × 2.5 cm glass fragment was removed from dense pleural adhesions. His postoperative recovery was uneventful, and he later returned to skydiving.

title: Application Effects of Modified Coronectomy in Mandibular Third Molars with High-Risk Proximity to the Mandibular Canal and Characteristics of Residual Root Migration
abstract: Abstract Objective To evaluate the perioperative outcomes, the protective effect on the inferior alveolar nerve, and the migration characteristics of residual roots within 12 months postoperatively following a modified coronectomy in cases of high-risk contact between the mandibular third molar root and the mandibular canal. Materials and Methods The study included 73 patients treated at the Department of Stomatology, First Affiliated Hospital of the Army Medical University, from November 2023 to July 2025. All patients underwent preoperative cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) scans and were divided into three groups based on the surgical procedure performed: the exodontia group (33 patients), the coronectomy group (5 patients), and the modified coronectomy group (35 patients). The primary outcome was postoperative sensation in the lower lip and chin, secondary outcomes included operative time, intraoperative blood loss, postoperative pain, facial swelling, limited mouth opening, temporomandibular joint clicking, and residual root migration. Clinical and radiographic follow-up lasted up to 12 months. Results The operative time in the modified coronectomy group was 51.30 ± 19.63 min, which was longer than the 32.97 ± 13.81 min in the exodontia group (P < 0.001); intraoperative blood loss was 15.07 ± 7.03 mL and 10.42 ± 5.88 mL, respectively (P < 0.05); Visual Analog Scale (VAS) scores on postoperative day 3 were 2.50 ± 0.75 and 3.09 ± 1.35, respectively (P < 0.05). No inferior alveolar nerve injury was observed in the modified coronectomy group, whereas the incidence in the exodontia group was 12.12% (P < 0.001); associated sensory abnormalities resolved approximately 3 months postoperatively. Residual root displacement increased with extended follow-up. At 12 months postoperatively, the migration distances for the groups with residual root lengths of ≤ 5 mm, 5–10 mm, and > 10 mm were 4.82 ± 0.59 mm, 3.06 ± 0.81 mm, and 4.13 ± 0.75 mm. After stratification by root morphology, the fusion root group exhibited more pronounced migration in the later stages, while the single-root group showed the lowest migration at 12 months. Conclusion In this study, no inferior alveolar nerve injury was observed in the modified coronectomy group, and postoperative pain scores were low. However, this procedure involved a longer operative time and relatively higher intraoperative blood loss. Residual root migration may be related to residual root length and root morphology, with 5–10 mm residual roots exhibiting relatively better stability during the 12-month follow-up period. Clinical Implications: For mandibular third molars where the root is closely associated with the mandibular canal and complete extraction may increase the risk of inferior alveolar nerve injury, modified coronectomy can serve as an alternative treatment strategy. During surgery, attention should be paid to the complete removal of enamel, control of residual root length, and preservation of alveolar bone, and standardized postoperative follow-up should be implemented.

title: MESNet: A Lightweight Transformer-CNN Collaborative Network with Morphology Awareness for Glioma Segmentation
abstract: Abstract Glioma segmentation is of great significance for clinical diagnosis and treatment, in which the effective utilization of multimodal information is crucial. Accurate segmentation holds substantial clinical value for guiding precise surgical resection, formulating personalized radiotherapy plans, and assessing prognosis. However, most existing methods focus primarily on the extraction and selection of deep semantic features while overlooking morphologically meaningful features such as edges and shapes. To address this issue, we propose a lightweight high-performance network named MESNet (Morphological Edge and Shape Network). MESNet is a Transformer–CNN collaborative segmentation model that explicitly imposes edge consistency and shape regularity to introduce morphological constraints, thereby enabling precise brain tumor segmentation. The model adopts an efficient 3D Transformer as its backbone, organically integrating convolutional neural networks to capture local details. Through deep complementarity between global context and fine-grained representations, it achieves accurate segmentation. To strengthen boundary awareness, a lightweight multi-scale edge-aware module is designed, which utilizes Sobel-based edge enhancement and spatial attention mechanisms to explicitly sharpen tumor boundaries, substantially reducing boundary errors without significantly increasing computational overhead. To accommodate irregular tumor morphology, an attention-guided shape-aware module is constructed; a zero-initialization strategy is employed to maintain training stability, and the module adaptively focuses on variations in tumor scale and shape, markedly improving the segmentation completeness and contour adherence of small targets such as enhancing tumors. Meanwhile, the network adheres to a lightweight design philosophy, strictly controlling parameter counts and computational complexity through channel compression and efficient attention mechanisms. Experimental results on the BraTS2021 dataset demonstrate that MESNet achieves overall segmentation accuracy and boundary agreement comparable to those of state-of-the-art methods while consuming substantially fewer resources, attaining a superior balance between efficiency and performance. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/tanjia123456/MESNet-main.

title: Primary malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor of the vagina: a rare case report
abstract: Abstract Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumor (MPNST) is an aggressive sarcoma typically arising from major nerve trunks in the trunk or extremities. Primary MPNST of the vagina is exceptionally rare, with very few cases reported in the literature to date. Herein, we report a rare case of a 67-year-old woman presenting with an 8-month history of vaginal bleeding and fluid discharge. Transvaginal ultrasonography revealed a solid mass (50*40*36 mm) on the posterior vaginal wall. The tumor was completely removed via radical surgical intervention, and the diagnosis of vaginal MPNST was confirmed through pathological examination and immunohistochemical analysis. Although adjuvant radiotherapy was recommended postoperatively based on clinical guidelines, the patient did not undergo this treatment. At the 3-month follow-up, gynecological examination and ultrasonography showed no signs of recurrence. However, one year after surgery, the patient presented with anal pain and discomfort. Pelvic MRI and CT demonstrated extensive recurrent masses in the pelvis and perineum, involving the rectum and anal canal with suspected anal fistula. Systemic evaluation indicated recurrence involving the posterior bladder wall and distal left ureter, resulting in mild left hydronephrosis, along with suspected metastasis to the right hepatic lobe. This case highlights the highly aggressive nature of primary vaginal MPNST and underscores the critical importance of adjuvant therapy and rigorous long-term surveillance for this extremely rare malignancy.

title: Intraoperative Inhalation of Indocyanine Green for Near-Infrared Visualization of Adult Intralobar Pulmonary Sequestration
abstract: Abstract Background The border between sequestered and normal lung in intralobar pulmonary sequestration (ILS) is often indistinct, complicating precise resection. Intravenous indocyanine green (ICG) can outline a perfusion-based boundary but requires prior control of the aberrant systemic artery and does not directly reflect the airway isolation that defines ILS. Case Presentation : Four adults with contrast-enhanced CT-confirmed ILS underwent video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery with intraoperative unilateral ICG inhalation. After single-lung ventilation, aerosolized ICG (2.5 mg/mL) was delivered via a nebulizer connected to the double-lumen tube for 10 to 15 minutes. Near-infrared thoracoscopy showed homogeneous fluorescence in ventilated normal lung and no fluorescence in sequestered tissue, producing a clear demarcation. Three patients underwent wedge resection; one with extensive basal segment involvement underwent lobectomy. No ICG-related adverse events occurred, and all patients recovered uneventfully. Conclusions Intraoperative aerosolized ICG inhalation safely and directly visualizes the ventilation-based boundary characteristic of adult ILS, enabling early lesion mapping and selection of the least extensive complete resection.

title: Normotension as a Red Flag: A Proposed Framework for Early Recognition of Masked Preeclampsia in Couvelaire Uterus – A Case Report and a Teaching Tool
abstract: Abstract Background Couvelaire uterus (CU) is a rare, life-threatening complication of placental abruption, occurring in about 1% of cases. Preeclampsia is a major risk factor; however, its diagnosis becomes difficult when concealed hemorrhage hides typical hypertension, delaying recognition. Additionally, the critical impact of the time from symptom onset to surgical intervention on uterine preservation is not well understood in the literature. title: Radiation-Induced High-Grade Glioma in a Long-Term Survivor of Medulloblastoma: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Advances in multimodal therapy have significantly improved survival in medulloblastoma, but long-term survivors remain at risk of secondary malignancies. We describe a rare case of radiation-induced high-grade glioma developing after a disease-free interval of approximately seven years, and nearly nine years following initial treatment. Case Presentation A 19-year-old male with a history of classical medulloblastoma (CNS WHO grade 4) presented nine years after his initial diagnosis with worsening headaches and fatigue. His primary tumor was treated with multiple surgical resections followed by high-dose craniospinal irradiation and adjuvant chemotherapy, after which he remained under surveillance. Seven years after completing treatment, he came in with a four-week history of weight loss and fatigue. One week before admission, he developed drowsiness, followed by a 10-day history of right focal seizures and increasing right-sided weakness. On neurological examination, he was obtunded with a Glasgow Coma Scale score of 9/15 and showed right-sided spastic hemiparesis with impaired verbal responsiveness. Magnetic resonance imaging revealed multiple supratentorial lesions associated with extensive vasogenic edema and mild midline shift, raising concern for a secondary malignant neoplasm. A left frontal burr-hole biopsy was subsequently performed. Histopathological examination demonstrated a highly cellular glial neoplasm composed of pleomorphic, hyperchromatic tumor cells embedded within a fibrillary background. Prominent microvascular proliferation and frequent mitotic activity were identified, consistent with a high-grade infiltrating glioma. Immunohistochemical analysis showed diffuse glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) positivity, absence of IDH1 R132H expression, retained ATRX nuclear staining, and a Ki-67 proliferation index of 15–20%. Tumor cells were negative for H3K27M, and mismatch repair protein expression was preserved. Based on the histopathological and immunophenotypic findings, a diagnosis of high-grade glioma, favoring astrocytoma, NOS, CNS WHO grade 4, was established. Given the patient's previous exposure to craniospinal radiotherapy and the prolonged latency period of nine years between treatment of the primary medulloblastoma and development of the high grade glioma, the lesion was highly suggestive of radiation-induced high-grade glioma. Despite supportive management, the patient's clinical condition deteriorated rapidly, and he succumbed to the disease one month after diagnosis. Conclusion This case illustrates the development of a secondary high-grade glioma in a long-term survivor of medulloblastoma, most likely representing a radiation-induced malignancy. It highlights the critical importance of lifelong surveillance in survivors of pediatric brain tumors, as early detection of secondary central nervous system neoplasms may allow timely intervention. Despite the limited therapeutic options available for these aggressive tumors, prompt recognition remains essential to optimize patient management and outcomes.
